1 لَسَدَ , aor.
لَسِدَ , (S, M, K,) and
لَسُدَ , (M,) inf. n. لَسْدٌ; (S;) and لَسِدَ, aor.
لَسَدَ , (S, K,) inf. n. لَسَدٌ; (S;) the latter mentioned by AHát, (S,) or Aboo-Khálid, (L,) in the Kitáb el-Abwáb, (S, L,) but the former is the more chaste, (TA,) It (a lamb or kid, K, or the young one of a clovenhoofed animal, S, M,) sucked its mother: (S, M, L:) or sucked her so as to exhaust all that was in the udder. (M, L, K.) ―
-b2- Also, both verbs, He (a dog) licked a vessel: (M, K:) or he (a man) licked what was in the vessel. (IKtt.) ―
-b3- Also, the former, He licked honey: (S:) and anything. (M.) You say لَسَدَتِ الوَحْشِيَّةُ وَلَدَهَا The female wild animal licked her young one. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
